record.paper_title: String Theory on ADS3: Some Open Questions
record.context_brief: modified current algebra or Sugawara construction
record.original_question: Can modifications of the affine Sugawara construction or of the SU(1,1) current algebra avoid the mass/spin cutoff and the conclusion that continuous representations describe only tachyonic excitations, while still describing the original string theory on AdS3 and also addressing infinite level degeneracy and modular invariance?

evidence.quote: Alternatively, we might also need a deformation of the affine Sugawara construction in order to lift the degeneracy without coupling to an external field. Modification of the current algebra itself has also been advocated.
The question then arises whether these deformations still describe the initial WZW theory.

one could try alternatively to avoid the mass/spin cut-off and the purely tachyonic continuous representations in various ways, playing essentially with the current algebra, and/or modifying the affine Sugawara construction.
it is not clear whether such modifications leave unaltered the interpretation of the theory as a string propagating over ADS3.
none of the available attempts treats the problem of the infinite degeneracy at each string level, or enlightens the issue of modular invariance.

artifact.category_tag: SL(2,R) WZW models and AdS3 string theory
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider bosonic string theory on AdS$_3$ formulated as a Wess–Zumino–Witten (WZW) model on the group manifold SU(1,1) (equivalently SL(2,$\mathbb{R}$)) at level $k$. The chiral algebra is the affine current algebra $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}(1,1)}_k$ generated by currents $J^a(z)$ ($a=\pm,3$) with OPE
$$ J^3(z)J^3(w)\sim -\tfrac{k/2}{(z-w)^2},\qquad J^3(z)J^\pm(w)\sim \pm\tfrac{J^\pm(w)}{z-w},\qquad J^+(z)J^-(w)\sim \tfrac{k}{(z-w)^2}-\tfrac{2J^3(w)}{z-w}, $$
and the worldsheet stress tensor is the standard affine Sugawara construction
$$ T(z)=\tfrac{1}{k-2}\!:\!\Big(\tfrac{1}{2}(J^+J^-+J^-J^+)-J^3J^3\Big)\!:(z). $$
With this construction, unitary normalizable physical states built from the discrete series $\mathcal{D}^\pm_j$ obey a mass/spin cutoff $j<(k-1)/2$ (the no-ghost bound), continuous principal series representations $\mathcal{C}^\alpha_j$ with $j=\tfrac12+i s$ contribute only purely tachyonic excitations to the physical spectrum, the spectrum exhibits an infinite level degeneracy of long-string-like states, and modular invariance of the one-loop partition function is problematic.

Question: Does there exist a deformation of the affine Sugawara stress tensor $T(z)$, or a modification of the SU(1,1) current algebra itself, such that all of the following hold simultaneously?
(i) The mass/spin cutoff $j<(k-1)/2$ is removed, allowing physical states of arbitrarily large spin.
(ii) The continuous representations $\mathcal{C}^\alpha_j$ contribute non-tachyonic physical excitations.
(iii) The infinite level degeneracy of the spectrum is lifted without coupling the theory to any external background field.
(iv) The resulting one-loop torus partition function is modular invariant.
(v) The deformed theory still admits an interpretation as the original WZW model describing string propagation on the AdS$_3$ target space.

Either construct such a deformation explicitly, or prove that no deformation satisfying (i)–(v) simultaneously can exist.
artifact.status_search_result: The SL(2,R) WZW description of strings on AdS3 was substantially clarified by Maldacena and Ooguri (2000–2001), who fixed the spectrum (including spectrally flowed long strings), proved a no-ghost theorem covering the relevant representations, and demonstrated modular invariance of the one-loop partition function, all within the standard affine Sugawara framework rather than via a deformation of it. This addresses several of the listed issues (modular invariance, role of continuous representations as long strings, level degeneracy via spectral flow) but does so without modifying the Sugawara construction or the current algebra. The specific question of whether a genuine deformation of the Sugawara construction or of the SU(1,1) current algebra can simultaneously achieve (i)–(v) while preserving the AdS3 string-theoretic interpretation does not appear to have a definitive resolution in the literature, so the original question is best classified as partially resolved/unknown.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS3 and the SL(2,R) WZW model. I: The spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: We study the spectrum of bosonic string theory on AdS3 ... and prove a no-ghost theorem for all the representations that are involved.
status_evidence.claim: Maldacena–Ooguri resolved the spectrum and no-ghost issues in the standard SL(2,R) WZW framework, including long strings from continuous representations and spectral flow.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS3 and the SL(2,R) WZW model. II: Euclidean black hole
status_evidence.snippet: the one-loop partition function ... is shown to be modular invariant
status_evidence.claim: Modular invariance of the AdS3 string partition function was established without deforming the Sugawara construction.
